questions.title: 小时候学到的新技能
questions.text:
Describe a new skill you learned when you were a child
You should say:
What the skill was
Who taught you this skill
How you learned it
And explain how you felt about learning the skill
questions.english:
A skill I learned as a child was typing on a computer. I learned it during primary school with help from my mother. It was a small skill, but it gave me more independence when using a computer.

At first, I had to look for each letter and used only a couple of fingers. My mother showed me how to place my hands and encouraged me to practise with short words rather than rushing straight into long passages.

I improved by doing a little practice regularly. I would type a few sentences, check the mistakes and try again. It was easier to notice progress when I compared my work with something I'd typed before.

I felt proud when typing became more natural. It meant I could write and look things up with less help. Looking back, that skill fits well with my current interests, because I now enjoy programming and spending time on computers. It shows how a simple childhood skill can become the starting point for a much bigger interest, even if the early practice wasn't particularly exciting.
questions.chinese:
可以描述的一项童年技能是电脑打字。我在小学阶段由母亲帮助学习。虽然是小技能，却让我使用电脑时更独立。

开始时，我必须寻找每个字母，而且只用一两根手指。母亲教我如何摆放双手，并鼓励我先练短单词，而不是急着输入长文章。

我通过定期进行一点练习来进步。我会输入几句话，检查错误，再重试。与以前打过的内容比较时，更容易发现进步。

打字变得自然时，我很自豪。这意味着我能更少依靠别人来写东西和搜索信息。回头看，这项技能很契合我现在的兴趣，因为现在我喜欢编程和使用电脑。它能说明，一个简单的童年技能如何成为更大兴趣的起点，即使初期练习并不特别有趣。
pending: 童年学习打字、母亲教授、练习过程全部为候选；确认或替换后作为个人经历使用

questions.title: 喜欢拍照的人
questions.text:
Describe a person you know who really likes taking photos
You should say:
Who the person is
When and how you got to know him/her
Where he/she takes photos
And explain how you feel about him/her
questions.english:
A person I'd describe as enjoying photography is a friend from university. We met through our studies and became friends because we both liked talking about technology and creative interests.

They take photos in ordinary places, such as streets, parks and the campus. They are interested in small details, like the way light falls on a building or how a familiar place looks at a different time of day. They don't need every picture to be taken somewhere famous.

When we go out, they sometimes stop to take a photo and explain what caught their attention. At first, I might not notice the same thing, but looking at the picture helps me understand their point of view.

I like this interest because it encourages people to pay attention to their surroundings. I'm more used to thinking through problems with a computer, so photography would offer a different kind of observation. I wouldn't mind waiting a little while they take pictures, as long as we still have time to enjoy the place together.
questions.chinese:
我想描述的一位摄影爱好者是我大学时的朋友。我们在学习中认识，也因为都喜欢聊技术和有创意的爱好而成为朋友。

这位朋友会在街道、公园、校园等普通地方拍照，关注细节，例如光照在建筑上的方式，或熟悉的地方在不同时间呈现的样子。照片不必都拍于知名景点。

一起外出时，这位朋友有时会停下来拍照，解释是什么吸引了自己的注意。开始时，我可能看不到同样的细节，但照片能帮助我理解对方的视角。

我喜欢这种兴趣，因为它鼓励人们注意周围环境。我更习惯用电脑思考问题，因此摄影能提供另一种观察方式。只要仍有时间一起享受这个地方，我不会介意等一会儿让朋友拍照。

questions.title: 小时候学到的新技能
questions.text: Is it important for everyone to have a specialized skill?
questions.english: A specialized skill can give someone useful career options and a stronger sense of competence. Programming, for example, allows people to build tools rather than only use them. However, not everyone needs to become an expert in a narrow field. Communication, adaptability, and everyday problem-solving also matter. A useful combination of skills may be better than specialization alone.
questions.chinese: 专项技能能提供有用的职业选择，并增强胜任感。例如，编程让人能构建工具，而非只使用工具。但不是每个人都必须成为狭窄领域的专家。沟通、适应性和日常解题也重要。有用的技能组合可能优于单一专业化。

questions.title: 小时候学到的新技能
questions.text: Can a child learn skills from another child?
questions.english: Yes, children often learn by watching and copying one another. A child who understands a game or a simple computer task can explain it in familiar language. Learning from a friend may also feel less intimidating. However, children can pass on mistakes, so an adult should provide guidance when safety or accurate information is important.

questions.title: 小时候学到的新技能
questions.text: Do you think it is easier for children to learn new skills than for adults?
questions.english: Children may pick up new sounds or movements quickly because they practise through play and aren't always afraid of mistakes. Adults, however, can use experience and set clear goals. For a complex skill like programming, that can be a real advantage. So children aren't automatically better learners; the type of skill and the learning conditions both matter.

questions.title: 小时候学到的新技能
questions.text: What are the differences between the way adults learn and the way children learn?
questions.english: Adults often want to know why a skill is useful before investing their time in it. They may use plans, instructions, and previous knowledge. Children are more likely to explore through games and imitation. Of course, these aren't fixed rules. An adult can learn through play, and a child can benefit from a clear explanation too.

questions.title: 小时候学到的新技能
questions.text: What skills should children learn before they go to school?
questions.english: Basic independence and social skills are more useful than advanced academic knowledge at that stage. Children should practise expressing their needs, taking turns, and asking for help. Simple tasks like washing their hands and looking after their belongings also matter. These skills make the classroom less confusing and help children feel comfortable around teachers and other children.

questions.text: Why do tourists like taking photos while they are travelling?
questions.english: Photos help tourists keep memories of places they may never visit again. They can also share the experience with family and friends who stayed at home. Sometimes taking a photo encourages people to notice interesting details, such as a building's design. Still, if they photograph everything, they may spend more time looking at a screen than enjoying the trip.

questions.title: 喜欢拍照的人
questions.text: Do you think it’s ok to take photos everywhere?
questions.english: No, some places need clear limits. Hospitals may protect patients' privacy, and museums may restrict photography to protect objects or improve the visitor experience. People should also ask before taking close photos of strangers. Being able to take a picture doesn't automatically mean it is appropriate. Respecting signs and people's comfort should come before getting an interesting shot.
